bull_case_summary: Microsoft has CFO rising to $182.935bn, $66.987bn annual cash FCF and 22% adjusted EPS growth. Round two argues these support internally funded compounding at 30.63x adjusted annual earnings despite nearly doubled capex.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts justified ownership and funding sufficiency but notes FCF declined 6.5% as earnings grew. Lease/noncash demands and overbought entry increase reliance on subsequent capacity productivity rather than invalidating the measured operating thesis.
key_points_of_agreement: Operating growth and substantial internal funding are verified.
Cash FCF is narrower than all-in equipment and lease commitments.
Cash conversion weakened despite earnings growth.
key_points_of_disagreement: How far funded compounding compensates premium valuation and increasing capital intensity, especially for aggressive adding.
unresolved_uncertainties: Detailed future lease/noncash equipment schedules for an all-in owner-cash forecast.
